children: Jupiter Wagons shares will remain in focus on November 25 after the company entered into a joint venture with South Korea-based Woojin Industrial Systems Co. Ltd.
Under the agreement, Jupiter Wagons will hold an 80 percent stake in the joint venture, while Woojin will own the remaining 20 percent.
The joint venture marks Jupiter Wagons' entry into two technology-intensive segments of rolling stock — complete metro coaches and propulsion systems.

The venture will manufacture complete metro coaches in India, along with critical components from Woojin's portfolio, including propulsion systems, Train Control and Management Systems (TCMS), automatic door systems, bogies and aluminium car body shells.
Catch all the market action on our live blog

On November 20, Jupiter Wagons received a repeat Letter of Intent (LoI) worth Rs 128.61 crore, including GST, from JSW (South) Rail Logistics Private Limited for the manufacture and supply of five BFNSM1 rakes comprising 302 wagons.

This is the company's second BFNSM1 order from the same customer, following an order worth Rs 122.88 crore in June 2026. With the latest order, Jupiter Wagons' cumulative order intake from the JSW Group in 2026 has reached approximately Rs 399 crore.
The company reported a marginal 1.83 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 46.15 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 45.32 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
In the previous trading session, the share closed at Rs 185.39, down Rs 5.84, or 3.05 percent.
The share touched a 52-week high of Rs 358.20 and a 52-week low of Rs 169.50 on 23 December, 2025 and 26 October, 2026, respectively.
Currently, the stock is trading 48.23 percent below its 52-week high and 9.41 percent above its 52-week low.
The company's market capitalisation stands at Rs 7,923.02 crore.

title: Jupiter Wagons shares in focus after entering JV with South Korean firm Woojin
